title: Decision record frontmatter, schema v1
$comment: Validated by scripts/check-decisions.mjs, and only for records carrying `schema: 1`. A record without that key is skipped ONLY when docs/decisions-baseline.txt lists it, unchanged — it predates the schema and is frozen; changing it means converting it to v1 first. Not listed, or listed and edited, fails. The `topic` enum is injected at validate time from docs/decisions/_config.json — deliberately absent here, because a topic list baked into a shared schema is a project-specific fact in a file that is not. Same reason nothing here names a repo: this file is byte-identical everywhere it is installed, so a sentence about one project's corpus is false in all the others.

schema.$comment: The gate. Its presence is what opts a record into validation at all.

topic.$comment: enum injected at validate time from docs/decisions/_config.json

ruling.$comment: The only field the operator reads. One sentence, plain English, no jargon.

revisit_if.$comment: The condition that makes this record worth re-opening, written so a person can tell whether it has fired. Required, and that is the whole point. `status` and `superseded_by` are how a record is *marked* retired; nothing but this field says what would *cause* anyone to go and mark it. An optional expiry is one nobody writes, and the corpus then accumulates until most of it is dead and none of it is trusted. Measured once at 78%, still being cited.

amends_spec.$comment: The DEC→SPEC leg, unchanged by schema v1. Absent from the v1 sketch, but gen:decisions writes the spec pointer from it and check() verifies the pointer landed — forbidding it here would break that for every rewritten record that amends the spec.
